body.statement:
For every admissible pair \(n\geq2\) and \(k\geq0\),
\[
 D_k(n)=2^{k+1}
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 n\geq2k+4.
\]
More precisely, if \(n<2k+4\), then
\[
 D_k(n)\leq\vartheta_{n-1,k+1}<2^{k+1}.
\]
Thus the exact values in the remaining below-threshold strip are left open; in particular, no equality between \(D_k(n)\) and \(\vartheta_{n-1,k+1}\) is asserted there.
body.proof_tex:
Fix an admissible pair \(n\geq2\) and \(k\geq0\).  If \(n\geq2k+4\), then \(\mathrm{thm:large\mbox{-}size\mbox{-}frontier}\) gives
\[
 D_k(n)=2^{k+1}.
\tag{36}
\]
Suppose instead that \(n<2k+4\).  Apply \(\mathrm{prop:joint\mbox{-}orientation\mbox{-}maximality\mbox{-}threshold}\) with \(N=n-1\) and \(g=k+1\).  Since
\[
 n<2k+4
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 n-1<2(k+1)+1,
\]
that proposition gives \(\vartheta_{n-1,k+1}\ne2^{k+1}\).  The upper bound in \(\mathrm{lem:joint\mbox{-}orientation\mbox{-}frontier}\) gives \(\vartheta_{n-1,k+1}\leq2^{k+1}\); because both sides are integers, it follows that
\[
 \vartheta_{n-1,k+1}<2^{k+1}.
\tag{37}
\]
Finally, \(\mathrm{thm:orientation\mbox{-}upper\mbox{-}bound}\) yields
\[
 D_k(n)\leq\vartheta_{n-1,k+1}<2^{k+1}.
\tag{38}
\]
Equations (36) and (38) prove both implications and the claimed strict submaximality.  Since (38) is only an upper inequality, it supplies no equality between the structural frontier and the combinatorial orientation frontier below the threshold.
